subject: economics
title: Elasticity and Surplus
welcome_lead: Measure responsiveness with elasticities - measure welfare with surplus.
meta_desc: A-Level Microeconomics: PED, PES, YED, XED and consumer/producer surplus.
final_note: Elasticities turn vague language into precise numbers.

concepts.def: Price elasticity of demand = percent change Q / percent change P.
Area between price and demand curve.
Area between price and supply curve.

walkthroughs.body_html: An absolute PED below 1 is inelastic, above 1 elastic. YED above 1 marks luxuries, below 0 inferior goods. XED positive means substitutes, negative means complements.
Consumer surplus is the triangle between the demand curve and the price line. Producer surplus is the triangle between the price line and the supply curve.
Taxes, monopolies and price ceilings create deadweight loss - surplus lost to neither party. Welfare analysis lives or dies by surplus measurement.

mcqs.q: What does price elasticity of demand measure?
options: PED measures how flexible or stretchy a product is.
The responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in price — the percentage change in quantity divided by the percentage change in price.
Consumer surplus is the profit that consumers make.
PED measures whether a product is expensive or cheap.
Consumer surplus is leftover stock that consumers haven't bought yet.
Consumer surplus is the profit that consumers make.
YED measures how the rich and poor differ in tastes.
The difference between what consumers are willing to pay and what they actually pay — represented by the area below the demand curve and above the price line.

mcqs.q: What does Income Elasticity of Demand (YED) tell us?
options: YED measures how the rich and poor differ in tastes.
A negative YED means the demand calculation went wrong.
The sign tells us the good type: positive YED = normal good (rises with income); negative YED = inferior good (falls with income). YED > 1 indicates a luxury; YED between 0 and 1 a necessity.
Consumer surplus is the profit that consumers make.
